scope: 0.15 source/CI/dependency and operator-tool security review. No security guarantee or complete penetration test. Public application remains a static site without a Node server, account, checkout, public write API or database.

findings.title: External link-check tool automatically followed unvalidated redirects/DNS
findings.surface: Operator/CI CLI, not a visitor-callable application endpoint
findings.before: scripts/check-external.mjs used fetch redirect:follow, without restricting redirect destinations or the resolved IP addresses. A changed remote source could direct an operator-run GET to a private or insecure destination.
findings.after: Node-only safe-outbound transport checks public HTTPS syntax at every hop; resolves all A/AAAA addresses and rejects any non-public result; pins those checked results in the socket lookup; uses an isolated direct TLS-verifying agent without environment proxies; bounds redirects/deadline/headers and discards bodies at headers.
limits: The IP policy is conservative; some legitimate special-purpose addresses may require manual review. No unsafe-network bypass is provided.
DNS and TLS trust remain dependent on the operator OS and supported Node runtime.
Unreachable or policy-blocked URLs are review items; they do not establish shop closure or stock.

findings.title: Local Node security patch floor lagged the official security release
findings.before: Project minimum and machine default allowed24.22.1. pnpm audit does not audit the Node executable.
findings.after: Minimum>=24.22.3; Astro command wrapper and CI reject lower stable versions. CI resolves latest24 patch with check-latest and checks the floor before package bootstrap. Official portableNode24.22.3 was SHA256-checked for task-local verification, without changing OS-global Node or PATH.
limits: The engine floor is a minimum, not a promise that every future runtime is free of vulnerabilities.

The bundled standalone pnpm launcher initially used a separate old Node. A task-local pnpm.cmd now invokes its existing11.25.0 JS CLI with the verified24.22.3 node.exe; nestedpnpm uses the same PATH wrapper. No machine-global launcher was modified.

findings.title: Dependency vulnerability auditing was not a CI deployment gate
findings.before: Frozen lockfile and weekly update configuration existed, but deploy workflow did not run the registry advisory audit.
findings.after: CI now runs pnpm audit --audit-level=low after frozen installation. No ignore/ignore-unfixable/ignore-registry-errors bypass was added. No dependency package or lockfile change was needed for the current zero-advisory snapshot.

reviewedBoundaries.observation: Existing safeHttps rejects credentials, literal IP/local names, ambiguous control/backslash syntax and nonstandard ports; merchant/affiliate hosts match exactly, and both approval states plus verified date gate sponsored links. Existing negative tests pass.

Browser code uses text/attribute assignments and native controls. The only set:html site sink is serializeJsonLd, which escapes markup delimiters and line separators; the existing script-close injection test passes. Markdown/source editors remain trusted code/content authors.

No CSP relaxation was required. Existing strict self/hash policy remains, Google iframe origin is bounded and its reviewed URL guard remains. Maps still requires a separate explicit display action; Google ad serving remains locked off.

Actions remain full-commit pinned. Checkout persist-credentials:false, read-only build token, privileged deployment isolated to deploy job, no untrusted pull_request_target/workflow_run checkout or interpolated user input found. No account settings were changed.

reviewedBoundaries.method: Signature subset via git grep -lI; file names only, never matched secret text. Current tracked working-tree text, not a complete history or generic-secret audit.
limits: A zero match is not proof that no secret exists. Ignored .env content, external account settings and full Git history were not inspected.

dependencyAudit.command: pnpm audit --json through task-local patched-node pnpm JS wrapper
dependencyAudit.interpretation: Zero known package advisories at this time. This is separate from Node executable advisories and does not guarantee no vulnerabilities.

runtime.installationScope: Task-local executable only; machine-global Node/PATH/OS settings unchanged.
runtime.signatureScope: SHA256 compared against official HTTPS SHASUMS256.txt. No independent PGP signature verification claimed.

baselineObservation.method: Read-only GETs of two fixed publicURLs. Redirects are not automatically followed. No request to a private target or account setting change.
baselineObservation.scope: Live0.14 public baseline before0.15 deployment; not a promise of future headers.

observedProtections: HTTP redirects to the matchingHTTPS URL
interpretation.riskBoundary: Absent headers are defense-in-depth gaps on this static site; no account/form/publicwriteAPI exploit was demonstrated. MetaCSP is not equivalent to HTTPframe-ancestors. No JSframebusting substitute or hosting migration was performed.

remaining: Observed the exact liveURL through manualredirect GETs: HTTPS200 and matchingHTTP→HTTPS301, HSTS and HTMLmetaCSP/metaReferrer are present; HTTP CSP/frame-ancestors, XFO, nosniff and Permissions-Policy are absent. These are defense-in-depth gaps, not a demonstrated account/form/publicwriteAPI exploit on the static application.
Meta CSP cannot enforce frame-ancestors. No false clickjacking/header-fix claim or ineffective meta header substitute was added.
MFA, collaborators, branch protection, account recovery and provider/platform controls require operator account settings; not changed or re-certified in this task.

sources.supports: Official24.22.3 is a security release dated2026-11-11, including HTTP/TLS/HTTP2 and other fixes.
Official SHA256 for win-x64/node.exe matched the task-local binary; independent PGP verification is not claimed.
Audit queries package advisory data; a matching remaining advisory at the configured level returns a failing status. This does not audit Node itself.
dns.lookup all:true exposes all returned address/family records for validation.
Version-specific HTTPS request/Agent API and lookup support; direct transport was independently smoke-tested on the verified24.22.3 binary.
Automatic redirect following can bypass destination validation; domain resolution introduces internal-address/DNS-rebinding concerns.
Special-purpose IPv4 ranges inform the conservative non-public address policy.
Special-purpose IPv6 ranges inform the conservative global-unicast policy.
Meta CSP does not support frame-ancestors; delivery is not equivalent to an HTTP CSP header.
Least-privilege token permissions, immutable action references and avoiding untrusted checkout/script injection are reviewed separately from package audit.

limits: No complete/zero-vulnerability or security approval guarantee.
No dependency audit result certifies account/platform security, all transitive source behavior or future advisories.
App/frontend security boundaries and operator-tool runtime fixes are distinguished.
